history.hpi: Patient reports feeling progressively weak and lightheaded over the past hour while gardening. Denies chest pain or shortness of breath. States it feels like her heart is 'beating really slow.' No prior episodes like this.
history.lastOralIntake: Breakfast and coffee approximately 3 hours prior
history.events: Husband found her sitting on the ground in the garden, pale and weak; called 911 immediately

scene.location: Single-family home, back garden, patient seated on the ground near a flower bed
scene.safety: No hazards to crew; uneven grass terrain near the garden bed
scene.bystanders: Husband present, witnessed her become weak and sit down; called 911 immediately
visualCues: Patient pale, seated on the ground

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 68-year-old female seated on the ground, pale and diaphoretic, alert but weak. Radial pulse is slow and thready.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, speaking in full sentences slowly
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse weak and slow, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all extremities, generalized weakness reported
otherFindings: Heart rate palpated at approximately 40 bpm
Reports feeling light-headed, worse when attempting to stand
No chest pain or shortness of breath
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I just feel so weak, my heart feels like it's beating really slow."

expectedActions.shortAction: Administer supplemental O2 titrated to 94-98% saturation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer oxygen as appropriate with a target of achieving 94–98% saturation
expectedActions.rationale: Maintains adequate oxygenation while the underlying rhythm is addressed.

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate cardiac monitoring and obtain 12-lead EKG
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms the rhythm as third-degree AV block and rules out concurrent ischemia.
Needed for atropine, sedation, and any subsequent vasopressor support.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood glucose and treat hypoglycemia per the Hypoglycemia Guideline and Hyperglycemia Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: Rules out a reversible metabolic cause of altered perfusion/weakness.

expectedActions.shortAction: Atropine 1 mg IV; may repeat every 3-5 minutes (max total dose 3 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Atropine 1 mg IV q 3–5 minutes (maximum total dose of 3 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: First-line pharmacologic therapy for symptomatic bradycardia, though third-degree block is often refractory.

transitions.condition: Crew completes a full assessment, establishes IV access, checks blood glucose, and administers atropine 1 mg IV per protocol for symptomatic bradycardia.

phases.name: Assessed and atropine given
phases.description: Crew completes the initial assessment, establishes IV access, checks blood glucose, and administers atropine per protocol. Given the complete heart block and the patient's home metoprolol, response is expected to be limited.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing symptomatic third-degree AV block, the crew establishes IV access, checks blood glucose, and administers atropine 1 mg IV; because the block is complete (and the patient takes a beta-blocker at home), atropine produces little to no improvement.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse remains weak and slow, skin pale and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Atropine 1 mg IV given, no significant change in rate
Patient increasingly anxious about persistent weakness
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That didn't seem to help much, did it?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 70 mcg IV for pacing analgesia (70 kg x 1 mcg/kg; max initial 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Transcutaneous pacing is painful; protocol calls for sedation/analgesia before pacing.

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate transcutaneous pacing, titrating rate and current to achieve capture
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transcutaneous Pacing – If pacing is performed, consider sedation or pain control
expectedActions.rationale: Definitive prehospital treatment for atropine-refractory symptomatic third-degree block.

transitions.if: Atropine fails, TCP with sedation performed
transitions.condition: Atropine produces no meaningful improvement, consistent with third-degree AV block; crew proceeds to transcutaneous pacing and administers fentanyl for analgesia/sedation before initiating pacing.
Crew proceeds directly to transcutaneous pacing without administering any analgesia or sedation first, contrary to protocol guidance.

phases.name: Atropine fails, TCP with sedation performed
phases.description: Atropine has failed to improve the heart rate given the complete heart block. Crew proceeds to transcutaneous pacing, administering fentanyl for analgesia/sedation before initiating pacing per protocol.
phases.triggerCondition: Atropine 1 mg IV produces no significant change in heart rate or perfusion, consistent with third-degree AV block. Per the protocol's guidance to consider sedation or pain control with pacing, the crew administers fentanyl and then initiates transcutaneous pacing.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulse weak and slow, skin pale and diaphoretic
otherFindings: Fentanyl given prior to pacing pad activation
Patient coached on expected sensation from pacing
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Okay, I'm ready if it will help."

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport in position of comfort; reassess vitals, pain, and pacing capture serially
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transport in position of comfort and reassess as indicated
expectedActions.rationale: Ensures continued mechanical capture and adequate analgesia are maintained en route.

transitions.condition: Transcutaneous pacing achieves electrical and mechanical capture at a paced rate, improving heart rate and perfusion; patient remains comfortable on fentanyl.

phases.name: Capture achieved, perfusion improved
phases.description: Transcutaneous pacing achieves consistent capture at a paced rate, improving heart rate and perfusion. The patient remains comfortable with fentanyl on board while the crew transports.
phases.triggerCondition: After pacing achieves electrical and mechanical capture, heart rate and blood pressure improve; the patient tolerates the pacing well with fentanyl analgesia on board.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial and pedal pulses stronger, skin warming, color improving
otherFindings: Mechanical capture confirmed with palpable pulse matching paced rate
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's much better, still a bit sore where the pads are."

phases.name: TCP performed without sedation
phases.description: Pacing is initiated without any analgesia or sedation. The patient experiences significant pain and distress from the pacing current, becoming agitated despite improving capture.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew proceeds to transcutaneous pacing without administering fentanyl or other sedation/analgesia first, contrary to the protocol's guidance to consider sedation or pain control with pacing.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Pulses palpable but patient thrashing, skin flushed
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Guarding and flinching with each paced beat, attempting to push pads away
otherFindings: Grimacing and vocalizing pain with each pacing spike
Blood pressure rising with pain/catecholamine response

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize pacing-related pain; give fentanyl 70 mcg IV rescue analgesia (70 kg x 1 mcg/kg; max 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Unsedated pacing is intensely painful and can cause the patient to resist care or dislodge pads.
